title: Cebu-based shipping firm denies hand in cigarette smuggling
summary: Cebu-based shipping firm Gothong Southern has denied involvement in the recently reported smuggling of P13 billion worth of cigarettes into the country.

blocks.text: Cebu-based shipping firm Gothong Southern has denied involvement in the recently reported smuggling of P13 billion worth of cigarettes into the country.
The company said it is not being probed in connection with the issue.

"In light of recent reports concerning the transportation of foreign cigarettes in alleged violation of customs regulations, Gothong Southern wishes to clarify that it is not currently the subject of any investigation in connection with this matter," the statement issued on Tuesday read.
"We respect due process and the authorities' role in establishing the facts," it added.
The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has filed charges against 13 individuals linked to the smuggling of cigarettes from China.

The bureau said the suspects will face charges for violation of the Agricultural Economic Sabotage Act after over 60 container vans carrying the smuggled cigarettes were found across several ports in Cebu.
The NBI also said it has filed cases against the big fishes in the case.
Moreover, the Gothong Southern assured that it is committed to moving the economy forward "with honest, accountability, and integrity."
"Our purpose is to move the economy forward through honest and lawful trade," it said. — VDV, GMA News
